verdict.rationale: TruffleHog offers indirect noise-reduction primitives — `--since-commit` to scan only new commits (baselining against history) and `--only-verified`/live-verification to suppress unverified false positives (trufflehog-docs-13, trufflehog-docs-1, trufflehog-gh-3) — plus detector allow/deny lists via `--include-detectors`/`--verify-detectors` (trufflehog-docs-7, trufflehog-docs-21). However there is no documented mechanism to mark/ignore a specific existing finding (e.g., a fingerprint-based baseline file or 'resolved' state) so it stops alerting on that exact finding going forward; the closest is a whole hosted platform 'track remediation status' feature (trufflehog-docs-17) which is described only at a high level with no detail on manual triage/ignore workflow. Missing for 10: an explicit ignore-list/baseline-file feature for specific findings, and independent confirmation that marking a finding as false-positive suppresses future alerts.
